sections.title: Architecture: Hub vs. Project
sections.content:
VenvHub Pro uses an architecture that strictly separates your source code from virtual environments. It is important to understand how this works under the hood:

  • Projects: The application only 'reads' folder names in your Projects Root. It never writes anything to these folders (except for on-demand requirements.txt or .vscode/settings.json for IDE integration).
  • Venv Hub: All virtual environments are physically stored in the central Venv Hub directory.
Advantage: If you accidentally delete an entire virtual environment, your source code (project) remains completely untouched. These two entities are physically separate on disk.

sections.title: Creation and Naming
sections.content:
When creating a new environment, the application enforces a strict naming convention and intelligently selects the engine based on the Python source.

Creation and Naming Process:

  1. Select a project (e.g. MyEshop) and a Python version (e.g. [Local] 3.12).
  2. Enter an environment name, e.g. My new version!.
  3. Your entered name passes through the internal sanitize_venv_name filter. The result will be: My_new_version!.
  4. The application creates a directory on disk inside the Hub folder named:
    MyEshop_My_new_version!.
What does sanitize_venv_name do?
This filter prepares a safe directory name for Windows. It replaces spaces with underscores and strips invalid characters (< > : " / \ | ? *), but intentionally preserves diacritics, exclamation marks, and non-Latin scripts (e.g. Cyrillic) for global compatibility.

Underlying Technologies (System vs. Local)

  • System Python: Uses the built-in venv module. This standard, reliable method creates a lightweight environment tied to your machine's primary Python installation.
  • Local Python (Embeddable): Uses the advanced virtualenv library. It creates a fully self-contained and isolated environment, ideal for portable use on USB drives.
Threading & Auto-Tools: The entire creation process runs asynchronously on a separate thread (QThread). Once created, VenvHub immediately installs setuptools and wheel into the new venv so that it is ready for error-free package installations.

sections.title: Row Actions and Process Management
sections.content:
Each row in the table represents one physical environment. The Actions column contains direct controls:

  • Radio Button (★): Sets the venv as default for the project and immediately synchronizes VS Code settings.
  • (Open in VS Code): Sets this Venv as default and immediately opens the project in VS Code with your active profile.
  • ▶ Play: Safely runs the assigned script via a temporary .bat file in the background, preventing errors caused by spaces in paths.
  • ■ Stop: Terminates the entire process tree (Kill Tree) via psutil and Windows Job Objects.
  • (Package Update): Triggers a bulk update of all outdated packages exclusively for this selected environment.
  • ✕ Delete: Safely deletes the entire virtual environment with a visual Progress Bar and cleans up stale paths from VS Code.

Right-Click and Double-Click Shortcuts

The environments table supports handy shortcuts:

  • Double-click a row: Instantly opens the full-featured Pip Manager window for the selected environment.
  • Right-click (Context Menu): Opens a menu with quick access to Pip Manager, Local Packages (Linker), Editable Packages (pip -e), and the Cloning feature.
What does the background Watchdog do?
It continuously monitors running scripts. If a script crashes unexpectedly (e.g. due to runtime code exceptions), the Watchdog detects it immediately and updates the UI state without freezing the application.

sections.title: Logical Linking and Scripts
sections.content:
Default Venv (Star ★)

A project can have multiple environments, but only one primary default. Setting an environment as 'Default' saves this association to venv_hub_pro_config.json. This setting is persistent and utilized by the Mini-Bar and VS Code integration.

Startup Script Selection (Validation)

Rule: You can only select an execution script physically located inside the project folder (validated via os.path.relpath) to ensure portability across USB drives.

sections.title: Cloning (Intelligent Reconstruction)
sections.content:
The 🐑 Clone / Backup Venv feature (right-click on a row in the Venvs table) is not a simple disk folder copy. Instead, VenvHub Pro performs a complete reproductive reconstruction:

5-Step Cloning Process:
  1. Freeze & Analysis: Runs freeze and separates packages into standard and editable (-e) dependencies.
  2. Clean Venv Creation: Creates a fresh environment base matching the parent Python runtime.
  3. Standard Package Installation: Bulk-installs all recorded packages.
  4. Editable Package Relinking (pip -e): For each editable package found, executes pip install -e <path>.
  5. Local Packages Migration (Linker Hook): Copies venvhub.json, venvhub_bootstrap.py, and the .pth hook file so that the clone immediately resolves identical local libraries.

Local Venv Cloning Strategies

Plan A (Fast): Uses the parent Python runtime referenced in the Birth Certificate.
Plan B (Fallback): If the parent runtime is missing, it installs virtualenv directly into the source environment and clones itself from within.

sections.title: Environment Birth Certificate (venv_birth_certificate.json)
sections.content:
Every environment created via VenvHub Pro includes an identification file named venv_birth_certificate.json. It acts as an identity document and persistent registry for the environment.

What Information Does It Contain?

  • Project Name: The project to which the environment is logically linked.
  • Python Version: The exact version used during creation (e.g. Python 3.12.4).
  • Source Python (source_python_path): The exact path to the parent Python runtime used for provisioning.
  • Live Package Manifest: A JSON list of installed packages and versions, automatically updated after every Pip Manager operation.
  • Creation and Modification Timestamps: Audit metadata for tracking and management.

How Does VenvHub Pro Use This File?

  1. Instant Cloning (Plan A): When cloning a portable venv, the app reads the original Python source path directly from this file to recreate an identical copy without reverse engineering.
  2. PyInstaller Builder: When building an executable (.exe), the Builder can package a comprehensive metadata manifest into the distribution.
  3. Diagnostics & Auditing: The About dialog reads these certificates to provide immediate insights into environment health and history.
Warning: This file is generated automatically by the application. Never delete it manually; otherwise, the environment loses its provenance metadata and cloning will have to rely on slower fallback strategies.

sections.title: VS Code Integration (Automatic Sync)
sections.content:
VenvHub Pro handles Visual Studio Code integration completely automatically via .vscode/settings.json located inside your project folder:

  • 1. New Environment Creation: If VS Code does not have an interpreter assigned, it automatically links the newly created environment.
  • 2. Default Environment Change (Star ★): Forces an update to settings.json (the python.defaultInterpreterPath key) and synchronizes local packages (python.analysis.extraPaths).
  • 3. Environment Deletion: Upon deleting a default venv, it cleans up stale interpreter paths in the editor configuration.
  • 4. Portable Mode & Drive Repair: When USB drive letters change, it silently updates paths in VS Code configuration files as well.

sections.title: Advanced Tools: VS Code Meta-Sync
sections.content:
If you create a package in the Local Packages folder containing a local_meta.json file with a vscode_integration section, VenvHub Pro will automatically merge predefined Tasks and Keybindings directly into .vscode/tasks.json and keybindings.json whenever linked, avoiding duplicate entries.

Advantage: You don't need to manually configure tasks.json in every new project. Just attach your local package to the environment and VenvHub Pro handles it for you.
